reference_summary: The PLC output triac U14 had an open anode due to a hairline solder fracture under its package. Contributing: the cabinet intake filter was 90% clogged, lowering airflow and raising the component temperature to 75°C. At 11:45:00, the top-oil temperature reached 70.1°C, which crossed the automatic fan-start setpoint. reference_summary: An errant 0.85 multiplier in the cooling control algorithm reduced the apparent oil-temperature input. That constant had been written during a firmware update thirty days earlier and never cross-checked. At 13:10, the outdoor heat wave caused the real top-oil temperature to exceed 82°C. The control system, however, calculated a top-oil value of 69.7°C at that same moment. By 13:18, the transformer's oil temperature continued upward to 91°C because fan airflow needs time. At 13:20, the high-oil-temperature alarm activated in the control room at exactly 90.0°C. Breaker 86G opened at 13:22:05, separating the generator unit from the grid and losing 178 MW of real power. An oil sample taken after the trip gave acetylene 23 ppm, thus indicating an incipient thermal fault. The controller's scaling constant was corrected to 1.00 and a firmware checksum check was installed. All cooling-control software parameter changes now require a second-person verification before upload.
